content.text: Dietary fiber is one of the most powerful — and underconsumed — nutrients in modern diets. It feeds beneficial gut bacteria, slows digestion to stabilize blood sugar, reduces LDL cholesterol, and is strongly associated with reduced risk of colon cancer.
Increase fiber intake gradually (add 3–5g per week) and drink plenty of water. Jumping to 38g per day too quickly can cause bloating and gas as your gut microbiome adjusts.

items.question: How much fiber should I eat per day?
items.answer: Women should aim for 21–25g per day and men for 30–38g per day. Most people consume only 10–15g — well below the recommended amount.

items.question: What are the symptoms of not eating enough fiber?
items.answer: Constipation, blood sugar spikes after meals, high LDL cholesterol, frequent hunger shortly after eating, and poor gut microbiome diversity are all common signs of insufficient fiber intake.
